summary: President Herzog is due to formally hand Eisenkot the mandate to form a government at the President's Residence on Sunday, Nov 8, at 5 p.m., after 67 MKs recommended him, 46 recommended Netanyahu and UTJ backed neither. Eisenkot says it is time for a national emergency government, and with the Arab-led parties ruled out his likeliest route runs through the Haredi parties, whom Liberman and Golan now say they could sit with on conditions such as Haredi enlistment. UTJ says it has not yet received an offer and its rabbis will decide, while Shas calls reports it could join an Eisenkot government fake news and says it remains in the right-wing bloc. Netanyahu responded to Herzog's decision by calling for a national unity government that includes all his current allies, which the Times of Israel describes as a likely non-starter.

phase.now: Herzog has chosen Eisenkot; the mandate is to be formally presented on Sunday, Nov 8, at 5 p.m. at the President's Residence
phase.next: Eisenkot then has 28 days to form a government, extendable by up to 14 days; if he fails, Netanyahu is next in line. The new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism in any future government and that the public does not want one dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List. Without a majority, he needs defectors or a new partner from the other side. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend any candidate, leaving Netanyahu without its endorsements, while Otzma Yehudit recommended him. Likud's delegation, last to meet Herzog, urged him to give Netanyahu the mandate, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 7 Herzog chose Eisenkot rather than Netanyahu to try first to form a government, Al Jazeera reports.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu and says he won't sit with him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president. Ynet reports Joint List and Ra'am leaders met in Nazareth on Nov 2 and will coordinate their recommendations. Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government relying on Arab parties, believing it would collapse. On Nov 3 Golan met Joint List leaders and they agreed to keep coordinating, while the Times of Israel notes the bloc's joint statement gave no indication of how it would govern without Arab parties. On Nov 4 Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot, while Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog a government cannot be formed with Arab parties. On Nov 5 the Joint List said it will recommend Eisenkot but will not formally join his coalition, offering possible outside support, Al Jazeera and ANI report. A Times of Israel analysis notes the Joint List has not said it will back an Eisenkot-led government.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am and said on Nov 2 he would oppose an Eisenkot minority government.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 2 Liberman declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ, saying the bloc will have to see what happens. Ynet reports on Nov 3 that Eisenkot is focusing on courting the Haredi parties and that Liberman has left the door open to talks on including them. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 3 that Shas and UTJ stress no decision has been made, with their rabbis due back around the start of consultations. On Nov 4 Shas recommended Netanyahu, and Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it would not compromise key priorities to bring Haredi parties in, Ynet reports. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend either candidate, with Goldknopf telling Herzog the party is not bound to any bloc, Ynet reports. ANI reports UTJ told Herzog its support for any government depends on legislation exempting yeshiva students from service. On Nov 5 Together told Herzog it will not accept a draft-evasion law, Israel National News reports. Channel 12 reports Liberman has dropped his refusal to sit with UTJ and that the opposition is in talks with it, but Yisrael Beiteinu told the Jerusalem Post it was not aware of this. Channel 12 reports the bloc is examining a coalition with UTJ and Shas, with draft talks starting from Liberman's 2018 bill, while Shas still stands with Likud. On Nov 6 Liberman said he is willing to be flexible and compromise on the Haredi draft law, the Jerusalem Post reports. The Times of Israel reports Liberman has confirmed he is open to a coalition with Haredi parties, reversing a key promise. After Liberman's shift, Eisenkot reiterated his demand for mandatory national service, the Times of Israel reports, and UTJ said it will back whoever solves the draft issue, Israel National News reports. UTJ leader Asher said on Nov 6 that no coalition proposal has yet been made to the party and that its rabbis will decide on any offer, the Times of Israel reports. Al Jazeera notes that adding UTJ and Shas would give Eisenkot a bare majority, as Herzog prepares to hand him the mandate. On Nov 7 Golan said he is open to a government with the Haredim on conditions including enlistment of young Haredim and no blank check, adding that they must come to meet his party in Ramat Gan. An unnamed Shas Council of Torah Sages source told Channel 12 that Shas would not act against UTJ's rabbis if they approve a deal, but Shas itself called reports it could join an Eisenkot government fake news, the Times of Israel reports.

blockers.text: Shas called reports it could join an Eisenkot government fake news and said it is part of the right-wing bloc.
Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman long pledged not to sit with Shas and UTJ, but on Nov 6 said he would compromise on the draft law.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.
Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it rejects compromising security and economic priorities to include Haredi parties.
Together told Herzog it will not accept a law exempting Haredim from the draft.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election. Ynet reports Netanyahu told associates privately he is not ruling out any option, including rotation, and that Katz says unity is off if the opposition ousts Speaker Ohana. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he is open to a broad government with any party that does not support terrorism but that he should lead it; an associate told Ynet no unity proposal has yet been made. Israel Hayom reports a Likud source's assessment, not a negotiated offer, that Netanyahu could accept unity if he served about two years and then became president, with Eisenkot taking over. ANI, citing the Times of Israel, reports Shas Council of Torah Sages member Rabbi Moshe Maya urged a unity government. On Nov 5 Yashar's delegation rejected a unity government with Netanyahu and called him the obstacle to unity, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 5 Likud MK Yoav Kisch urged a broad national government and called on the opposition to end its boycott, the Times of Israel reports. After Herzog's decision on Nov 7, Netanyahu called in a video for a national unity government including all his current allies, which the Times of Israel calls a likely non-starter. Kan reports, citing an unnamed associate, that Netanyahu would discuss rotation if unity talks were held, and that an envoy's approach to Eisenkot was rebuffed; Yashar said it knew of no such approach and that Likud can join an Eisenkot-led coalition without extremists.

blockers.text: Likud whip Ofir Katz said the party opposes a rotation of the premiership.
Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.
Together MK Merav Cohen warned against a unity deal with Likud, saying "You don't make deals with scorpions."

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: After Herzog chose Eisenkot, Netanyahu called in a Nov 7 video for a national unity government that includes all his current allies, the Times of Israel reports.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: Reacting to Herzog's decision on Nov 7, Eisenkot said it is time to form a national emergency government, while Yashar said Likud could join an Eisenkot-led coalition without extremists.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Together recommended Eisenkot to Herzog on Nov 5, with faction chair Ginzburg vowing to help him form a government quickly and MK Merav Cohen rejecting both a draft-exemption law and a unity deal.
red_lines: No government reliant on Arab parties (per Ynet)

אמת.stance: On Nov 7 Golan said he is open to a government with the Haredi parties if they accept conditions including Haredi enlistment and workforce integration.

ל.stance: On Nov 6 Liberman set out conditions for joining an Eisenkot-led coalition, saying he is ready to compromise on the Haredi draft law but rejecting a rotation with Eisenkot.

שס.stance: On Nov 7 Shas dismissed reports it could join an Eisenkot-led government as fake news and said it remains part of the right-wing bloc, the Times of Israel reports.

ג.stance: On Nov 6 UTJ leader Asher welcomed the new flexibility on the draft but said no coalition offer has been made and the party's rabbis will have the final say, the Times of Israel reports.

ב.stance: Otzma Yehudit recommended Netanyahu on Nov 5, and its delegation claimed without evidence that some votes were bought, Ynet reports.

ט.stance: Religious Zionism recommended Netanyahu on Nov 4, with its delegation arguing Arab nationalist parties are not legitimate partners in forming a government, Ynet reports.

עם.stance: Ra'am recommended Eisenkot to Herzog on Nov 5 and asked Speaker Ohana for an early vote on his successor, Ynet and the Times of Israel report.

ודם.stance: The Joint List announced a unanimous decision to recommend Eisenkot to Herzog, saying it will not formally join his coalition but may support it from outside, ANI reports.

timeline.text: Reacting to Herzog's choice, Eisenkot said it is time to form a national emergency government.
In a video after Herzog's decision, Netanyahu called for a national unity government that keeps all his current allies.
Golan set conditions for partnering with Haredi parties, saying "Whoever wants a partnership with us needs to come meet us in Ramat Gan."
Shas called reports that it could join an Eisenkot-led government fake news and said it is part of the right-wing bloc.
Herzog's office said the mandate will be presented to Eisenkot at the President's Residence on Sunday at 5 p.m.
Herzog told Eisenkot on Saturday evening that he will be tasked with forming a government, with the formal handover set for a Sunday ceremony.
Hours before Herzog's decision, Netanyahu warned that an opposition government relying on Arab-led parties would bring Israel's collapse.
Haaretz reports UTJ welcomed Liberman's reversal on the Haredi draft, though a coalition deal with the party is not assured.
In a pre-Shabbat statement, Eisenkot said he plans a government of the four Zionist parties in his bloc, open to others who accept his principles "now or later."
Asher welcomed the sudden flexibility on the draft but said UTJ has received no coalition offer and its rabbis will decide.
Golan said substantial progress has been made toward a national emergency government and that he is more optimistic than after the election.
UTJ said it will support whoever provides a solution to the draft issue, Israel National News reports.
Eisenkot reiterated his demand for mandatory national service after Liberman opened the door to a coalition with Haredi parties.
Eisenkot said significant progress has been made in coalition talks and warned that Netanyahu's continued caretaker government is dangerous.
Liberman confirmed he is open to a coalition with Haredi parties, going back on a key campaign promise, the Times of Israel reports.
Liberman laid out terms for joining an Eisenkot coalition, offering draft-law flexibility and saying rotation "must be consigned to oblivion."
After Herzog raised a unity deal, Yashar MK Shaul Meridor told him the public had sent the Oct. 7 government home, a Times of Israel analysis reports.
Herzog challenged Likud's Miri Regev for calling Eisenkot's camp a 'disaster bloc' while claiming to extend a hand.
Likud MK Yoav Kisch called for a broad national government of Zionist parties and urged the opposition to end its boycott and talk.
Channel 12 reports Liberman gave bloc partners a green light to negotiate with the Haredi parties, with draft talks based on his 2018 bill.
Herzog said the results may look clear but cited mutual vetoes between and within the blocs, and said he would hold personal talks with some party leaders before choosing on Sunday.
Herzog said Eisenkot received the most recommendations but that he will hand over the mandate only on Sunday, the Times of Israel reports.
Ra'am formally asked Speaker Ohana to hold a vote on his successor at the new Knesset's first session next week.
Likud's delegation, the last to meet Herzog, said the mandate should go to Netanyahu and warned against relying on the Joint List.
Yashar recommended Eisenkot, rejected a unity government with Netanyahu and said it would first negotiate with its bloc partners.
Channel 12 reports Liberman is now willing to sit with UTJ, ending his long-standing refusal.
Yisrael Beiteinu told the Jerusalem Post it was not aware of any change in Liberman's stance on Haredi parties.
Ynet tallies 67 recommendations for Eisenkot and 46 for Netanyahu once consultations ended, with UTJ backing neither.
Together MK Merav Cohen told Herzog the party rejects a draft-exemption law and warned against a unity deal with Likud.
Together recommended Eisenkot to Herzog, with faction chair Ginzburg pledging to help him form a government as quickly as possible.
